Definition: from G575 and G4724; set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively:--put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty).
BiblicalUsage: To send out on a mission is the heartbeat of this word. God sent His Son not to condemn the world but to save it, Jesus sent His disciples out two by two, and after the resurrection He sent them the same way the Father had sent Him. Sending always carries the sender's authority and purpose with it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe being sent is not a promotion, it is a commission. We go because we were sent, and the One who sent us goes with the message. That is what makes ordinary people able to carry the gospel anywhere.
